decision_scope: Independent review of the frozen offline opt-in v6 implementation only; not runtime or operational acceptance

shown.claim: Plan.load opts into worker shutdown only for schema v6; its appended dataclass flag defaults false. Existing v1-v5 schema branches retain their previous signal selection. This is bounded source inspection, not full legacy-suite proof.

v6 requires each service's exact direct python -m uvicorn command and rejects explicit entrypoint overrides. Backend image checks require an empty inherited entrypoint before per-image creation and credential collection. The new fixed commands and legacy command remain recognized without exporting arbitrary command text.

The embedded worker source validates the exact shell launch, one direct child, worker name, PPid, module, port, TERM dispositions, non-zombie state and start time. It opens a dynamic pidfd, revalidates identity, checks its budget and signals only through that handle. Handle cleanup runs on post-open failure; no numeric-PID fallback, group signal, forced stop or retry is present.

The original backend monotonic deadline includes pre-observation and command time. The fixed worker receives the remaining absolute wall deadline and derives a local monotonic bound; elapsed launch time is not intentionally refunded. Missing capability, malformed identity and observed budget violations fail closed under the documented clock assumption.

A fixed exact acknowledgement is necessary but insufficient for success. Backend and parent still require fresh stopped-original and unchanged-storage/identity checks. Missing or malformed acknowledgement leaves pending intent unresolved rather than inferring interruption ownership or triggering a retry. Restart retains its existing path.
v6 continuation validation requires the added worker source in the exact consumer set and verifies its digest; legacy consumer sets do not add it.

independent_test.command: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 ./.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest --noconftest -c /dev/null -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_companion_worker_shutdown.py
independent_test.scope: Only the new test file was selected, using the checkpoint isolation flags. Tests use synthetic procfs, pidfds, clocks and backend commands; no Docker or live signaling was invoked.
independent_test.not_proven: The full embedded program is compiled but not run against a kernel. The full legacy suite, runtime integration and end-to-end continuation loading were not independently executed. The checkpoint's earlier 509-pass result remains CLAIMED in this review.

material_assumptions: The pinned image and process tree are trusted; deliberately spoofed argv and hostile exec between validation and signal are outside this contract. A pidfd prevents PID-reuse redirection, not atomic executable-identity freezing.
Host/container wall clocks must be coherent for the remaining absolute deadline. This is a required runtime assumption, not independently established by offline tests.
unverified_runtime_risks: Installed Linux/Python pidfd APIs and kernel support remain UNVERIFIED.
Clock coherency and installed process argv/topology on all four original services remain UNVERIFIED.
Worker shutdown, shell/container exit and complete parent verification within the ten-second budget remain UNVERIFIED.
PID1 exit may terminate the exec before acknowledgement delivery; that remains an unresolved pending-intent failure even if the service has stopped.
Cancellation or transport loss does not establish ownership; this review does not provide live cancellation or recovery proof.
proof_required_before_any_separate_opera: Separately review current read-only pidfd, clock and exact per-service process-identity capability evidence.
Separately review fresh v6 manifest, replacement fingerprints, changed consumer bindings, preparation and runtime packet; do not reuse stale bindings or consumed attempt inputs.
Retain explicit unresolved-ack, pending ownership, bounded recovery and cancellation handling; no retry or forced stop is authorized by this record.
